verdicts.reviewer_notes: Third review, covering only the review2 fix (key_obligations[0], Article 101 exception) plus a full re-check of the entry. Re-fetched EUR-Lex CELEX:32024R1689 (primary). It confirms the title 'of 13 June 2024', OJ L 12.7.2024, status 'In force', and consolidated versions dated 12/07/2024 and 27/07/2026. Re-fetched consolidated Article 113 on the Commission AI Act Service Desk. It confirms entry into force on the twentieth day after publication (giving 2024-08-01) and general application from 2 August 2026. Chapters I and II apply from 2 February 2025, with limited exceptions from 2 December 2026, which are the new Article 5 prohibitions. Chapter III Section 4, Chapters V, VII and XII and Article 78 apply from 2 August 2025, 'except Article 101'. Annex III / Article 6(2) high-risk applies from 2 December 2027, Annex I / Article 6(1) from 2 August 2028, and Articles 102-110 from 27 July 2026. Re-fetched Article 101 on the Service Desk. Its title is 'Fines for providers of general-purpose AI models' and the fining body is the Commission, so the new parenthetical ('except Article 101 fines on GPAI providers, which apply from 2 August 2026') is accurate: excluded from the 2025 date, Article 101 falls to the general 2 August 2026 date. Re-fetched the 2026/1744 ELI page. It gives OJ L 24.7.2026 and entry into force on the third day after publication, i.e. 27 July 2026, which supports the 'amended' timeline entry and the consolidated-version claim. Amended Article 4 says providers and deployers must 'take measures to support the development of AI literacy', which matches key_obligations[2]. All four timeline dates match the sources, and status in_force is correct. Not a duplicate: Glob of content/instruments/ shows only eu-digital-omnibus-ai.json and eu-gpai-code-of-practice.json, content/items/ is empty, and the slug is unique in the file. Tone is neutral, with no predictions. Minor (non-blocking): the 2024-06-13 'passed' entry relies on the EU convention that the 'of <date>' in the title is the signature date. EUR-Lex shows the date in the title, not an explicit 'date of signature' label, so the note is acceptable.

Third review, covering only the review2 fixes (key_obligations[1] and the summary's last sentence) plus a full re-check. Re-fetched https://www.admin.ch/gov/en/start/documentation/media-releases.msg-id-104110.html (Federal Council, primary). It confirms the 12 February 2025 decision: 'Switzerland intends to ratify the Council of Europe Convention on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and to make the necessary amendments to Swiss law', and 'Work will also continue on the regulation of AI in specific sectors such as healthcare and transport.' The new key_obligations[1] matches this text and drops the unsupported 'rather than a horizontal AI law' inference. Re-fetched https://www.bk.admin.ch/en/artificial-intelligence (Federal Chancellery, primary). It confirms, verbatim, 'In Switzerland, there is not yet any overarching legislation that deals specifically with AI', which matches the revised final summary sentence. The FDJP with DETEC, the FDFA and other federal offices will 'draw up a bill on AI regulation to be submitted for consultation by the end of 2026', covering 'transparency, data protection, non-discrimination and supervision'. The non-binding measures implementation plan (industry solutions, voluntary commitment declarations) is due by end of 2026. 'The Federal Chancellery has also maintained a contact point for the Federal Administration since 1 February 2026.' Every summary and key_obligations claim traces to one of these two pages. Both timeline dates match. Status check: because a consultation opening before today would make 'proposed' stale, I searched in English and German for a Federal Council Vernehmlassung on the AI bill. I found no consultation opening. The search results (bk.admin.ch/de/regulierung, secondary commentary) still describe the consultation as due by end of 2026, so 'proposed' remains the closest enum. Not a duplicate: not in content/instruments/ or content/items/, and the slug is unique in the file. Tone is neutral. Minor (non-blocking, editor discretion): the 2026-02-01 timeline note mixes a dated event (contact point) with an undated forward deadline (bill and plan due by end of 2026). It is worded as a deadline, not a completed event, so it is not misleading. The 27 March 2025 Swiss signature of CETS 225 appears in a secondary search result (netzwoche/AlgorithmWatch-type sources) but remains correctly excluded until a primary source is fetched.
